explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/936: are 2^n ± 1 and n! ± 1 powerful for only finitely many n? Open unconditionally; known under abc (Cushing–Pascoe for n! ± 1, CrowdMath for 2^n ± 1). This case asks that 2^n + 1 be eventually not powerful, i.e. powerful for only finitely many n. Nat.Powerful is 2-full (p | m implies p² | m), as on the page. Truncated subtraction affects only n = 0. Faithful.
